genericProblem: A shared operations surface conflated selected data-node scope, UI action visibility, fact-owner boundaries, and server-side command authorization, so a persisted multi-scope session could be resolved to the wrong owner target, a coarse role key could be mistaken for owner-safe write authority, or a whole-save could be incorrectly split into two user permissions.

finiteDenominator.operations: All 42 catalog-inventory edge operations: 16 GET reads, 18 dual HEAD_COMPANY/STORE catalog writes, 8 STORE-only catalog-copy or inventory writes.
finiteDenominator.capabilities: The catalog role catalog, workspace session schema, P1 operation generator, generated edge wire, platform role editor, operations catalog/inventory pages, edge controller, application coordinator, catalog/inventory/production/asset owner command boundaries, role migration, API/L2/DEV fixtures.
finiteDenominator.counterexamples: PageAccess remains route admission rather than a write capability; public asset reads and ordinary inventory diagnostics are reads and therefore do not receive a capability key.

findings.finding: The catalog controller selected Store before Head Company from a session that can validly retain both, ignoring the explicit requested data-node reference and producing brand-workbench SCOPE_FORBIDDEN responses.
EDIT_CATALOG_LIBRARY conflated Head Company catalog, Store catalog, and Store inventory owner writes; READ_INVENTORY_ADVANCED_DIAGNOSTICS made a GET into a role capability.
Catalog-inventory mutation contracts advertised a UI capability but the edge, application coordinator, and owner command APIs did not live-recheck it or pass a server-minted owner scope grant.
The platform role editor required a non-empty capability set and the shared catalog drawer exposed Store-only local copy from the Head Company surface.

A review correctly found that scope-only owner grants let catalog whole-save reach inventory commands, but treating that as a requirement for a second inventory capability would contradict the approved one-save product task. The missing boundary was command purpose: only the catalog whole-save requirement may coordinate the two named inventory-definition commands; direct inventory workflows remain inventory-authorized.
